problem: What is the domain of the function  $f(x)=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{4}-\frac{\pi }{2})?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a General Expression for the Domain of a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function
examples.problem: What is the domain of the function $y=\tan\left(\dfrac x 2\right)?$
examples.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\tan x$ is given by the expression

$$
x \neq \dfrac\pi 2 + n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $\tan\left(\dfrac x 2\right),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left(\dfrac x 2\right).$ This gives

$$
\dfrac x 2 \neq  \dfrac\pi 2 + n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2} & \ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ x & \ne \pi +2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x \neq \pi + 2n\pi,$ where $n$ is an integer.

feedback.problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the vertical asymptotes of the function $f(x)=\operatorname{tan}⁡(8x)+\pi ?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
feedback.worked_solution:
The asymptotes of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ are given by the expression

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the asymptotes of $\operatorname{tan}⁡(8x)+\pi ,$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(8x).$ This gives

$$
8x=\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{16}+\frac{n\pi }{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the expression giving all the vertical asymptotes is $x=\frac{\pi }{16}+\frac{n\pi }{8},$ where $n$ is an integer.
